label: Bible Study
prompt: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be _____ among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
verse: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
note: The chief priests quoted this to Herod when the wise men asked where the king would be born.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: As a _____ seeketh out his flock in the day that he is among his sheep that are scattered; so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.
verse: As a shepherd seeketh out his flock in the day that he is among his sheep that are scattered; so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.
note: God goes looking for scattered sheep on 'the cloudy and dark day' — the exact day you'd get lost.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about _____ furlongs.
verse: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs.
note: Threescore furlongs is about seven miles — the Emmaus road walk where a stranger turned out to be Jesus.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the _____ of sins.
verse: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.
note: Love refuses to keep a ledger — Peter likely echoes Proverbs 10:12, 'love covereth all sins.'

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: No man that warreth _____ himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
verse: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
note: No soldier on duty 'entangleth himself' with civilian affairs — he aims to please the one who enlisted him.
